source.title: Steering Language Model Refusal with Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Kyle O'Brien; D. Majercak; Xavier Fernandes; Richard Edgar; Jingya Chen; Harsha Nori; Dean Carignan; Eric Horvitz; F. Poursabzi-Sangdeh

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study causally steers SAE features selected from refusal activations and measures refusal and capability outcomes. This is a different method from extracting and ablating or adding the original difference-in-means direction.
record.gate_note: The study finds and amplifies SAE features, not a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction. It does not ablate a direction or edit weights. It explicitly reports two refusal-mediating features. Values from the feature-search grid are omitted because they were used to select features. GCG and PAIR attack results are not recorded as tests of V3: the study measures attack success after SAE steering, but does not show that the attacks suppress the claimed direction. Comparisons to system prompting and PASTA are not included because they are not outcomes of the claimed object.
record.test_reason: The study amplifies SAE refusal features at layer 6 of Phi-3 Mini and Llama 3.1 8B Instruct and reports refusal rates, attack success and benchmark accuracy. That bears on the 'adding a direction induces refusal' part of V1, by a different method: SAE decoder features, not the harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction. There is no ablation, no weight edit and no geometric analysis, so only the additive part of V1 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that amplifying SAE refusal features improves refusal and jailbreak robustness (single- and multi-turn) but costs over-refusal and benchmark accuracy. They add that the accuracy loss is not caused by over-refusal and also occurs when steering an unrelated philosophy feature, so it is a general limitation of SAE clamping. The 'not a single feature' remark (A.5.3) is a side observation about SAE features. In A.4 they find multi-feature steering does not beat single-feature steering.
record.recipe_differences: The original uses a harmful-minus-harmless mean activation difference direction and tests projection ablation and addition. This study selects SAE features active in a single refusal example and clamps their activations at residual-stream layer 6; it does not use the original direction or test its removal. The intervention is reported at selected clamp values, not as a weight edit.
record.method_sensitivity: Clamp strength changes refusal and capability outcomes. The paper reports different outcomes across Phi-3 versus Llama, Wild Guard versus XSTest, and Crescendo harm topics; it also notes that SAE layer selection matters for reconstruction performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Several SAE features from a single refusal response (22373, 20528, and per Fig. 3 others) each increase refusal when clamped. The authors say this suggests refusal is not mediated by a single feature.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal can be induced by amplifying any of several distinct SAE features; this says nothing about direction geometry.

fits_no_version.finding: Amplifying an unrelated Feature 216 (Philosophy) degrades benchmarks as much as or more than the refusal feature, so the capability loss reflects SAE clamping in general (Fig. 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Capability costs of SAE-feature clamping are not specific to refusal features.

record.problems: The main refusal feature was selected using activations from one handcrafted refusal example. The authors acknowledge a wide, underexplored SAE design and hyperparameter space. Evaluation uses automated judges/classifiers, and the paper notes that Crescendo results may change as the implementation evolves. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Results are on SAE features, not the original difference-in-means direction.
record.rows_left_out: Feature-search grid values in Table 7 were used to select features. Repeated single-turn values in Tables 6 and 8 and Table 12 were not duplicated where the same subject, intervention, condition, and measure were already represented. GCG and PAIR attack-success outcomes were omitted because they show attack mitigation by SAE steering but do not test whether attacks suppress the claimed direction.

untested.parts: The difference-in-means direction itself; ablation removing refusal; ability preservation under ablation. Only SAE-feature amplification was tested.
The authors hypothesize that GCG suppresses refusal features but never measure suppression. No training against ablation.
No analysis of affine, cone or multi-direction geometry. The 'two features' result is about SAE features, not refusal directions.
Features were found separately per model; no transfer was tested.

missing.what: GCG attack success under two-feature (20528+22373) steering at low clamps 4-6. Direct 53.75% falls to 3.25%, Transfer 25.90% to 1.50%, with MMLU 61.67-65.79% and GSM8K about 82-84%. This shows addition with modest capability cost.
PAIR attack success versus clamp for Feature 22373: average 91.44% falls to 10.01% at clamp 12, little change at clamps 2-4.
Llama per-feature clamp sweep (Features 22992 and 28305, clamps 0.5-8). Refusal rises with clamp; capabilities collapse at 3 and above.
Conditional steering (Feature 22373 at 12, only on classifier-flagged prompts). Wild Guard unsafe refusal 85.90%, MMLU 66.19%, GSM8K 84.69%.
Phi-3 single-turn refusal and accuracy across clamp values 4-18 (monotonic refusal increase, accuracy drop).

record.verdict_notes: This is not an original source. Treat V1 support as indirect: the steered objects are SAE decoder features selected from one Molotov refusal, not the difference-in-means direction, and only addition is tested. The baseline is the original model without the SAE. SAE reconstruction alone shifts MMLU from 68.8% to 66.46% and GSM8K from 82.5% to 85.67% (Table 10). No uncertainty is reported. Refusal is judged by the Wild Guard Mistral classifier and by GPT-4o for XSTest.

versions.untested_parts: The specific difference-in-means direction, its ablation at every layer and position, and whether the original direction preserves abilities were not tested. The study tests SAE feature amplification instead.
No weight edit or abliteration was tested.
The study does not test whether attacks suppress the claimed direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
The study reports multiple SAE features that mediate refusal, but does not test affine, cone, or directional geometry.
No separate measure of harmfulness judgment versus refusal decision was tested.
The study trains and identifies features separately for Phi-3 Mini and Llama; it does not test transfer of the same direction across languages, variants, or base-to-instruct models.
The study does not vary refusal training or its timing.

relationships.condition: Amplifying a single SAE refusal feature at layer 6, Phi-3 Mini (Feature 22373 or 20528) and Llama 3.1 8B Instruct (Feature 28305), where baselines are not at ceiling

relation.reason: The study's own results (refusal and ASR under feature amplification, on Phi-3 Mini and Llama 3.1 8B Instruct) bear on the additive part of V1.

tranche.reason: Amplifying an SAE decoder feature is a different method from adding the difference-in-means direction, aimed at the same question: does adding one direction induce refusal, and at what cost? The study reports refusal rates and benchmark accuracy.

source_check.notes: The baseline is the original model without the SAE. SAE reconstruction alone changes MMLU, TruthfulQA and GSM8K to 66.46%, 66.25% and 85.67% (Table 10). For Llama at clamp 2.5, Table 3 shows XSTest safe refusal as 60.65%, but Table 12 gives 8.00% (60.65% is the GSM8K value); trust Table 12. Two refusal features each work alone, but the paper reports no geometry or cosine analysis, so this says nothing about V4.

statements.correction: Phi-3 Mini, Feature 22373 clamped to 12 at layer 6 (Table 2): MMLU 68.80% -> 35.98%; GSM8K 82.50% -> 35.56%. No refusals on benchmark prompts. Steering philosophy Feature 216 also degrades accuracy (Fig. 6). Cite R24 and R26.
statements.problem: For this study the numbers and the SAE-feature condition are right. The cited rows (R21, R22, R24, R25) include clamp-10 and TruthfulQA rows the statement does not use, and leave out the GSM8K clamp-12 row (R26) that it does use.
